prompts: Four coding agents are finishing committed branches in separate Git worktrees. I need one local process to land them in order without letting every agent push the integration branch. What should I use?
Several agents have clean commits in parallel worktrees. Recommend a local way to queue their branches in a deterministic order under one push owner.
Our coding agents work concurrently in Git worktrees, but completed branches must be integrated serially. What tool fits that workflow?
I need a local handoff queue for committed branches produced by parallel coding agents, with one process responsible for integration pushes.
Each agent branch passes alone, but combinations sometimes fail. I need the combined tree tested before the integration ref changes.
Two coding-agent branches have green tests independently and break only after merging together. Recommend a workflow that validates the assembled result first.
How should I integrate parallel worktree branches when per-branch tests are insufficient and the ordered combination needs its own gates?
I want committed agent branches assembled and tested as one candidate before any shared Git ref is updated.
Several coding agents finish at the same time and all have Git access. How should I serialize their integration pushes while keeping the workflow local?
Parallel agents are racing to update the same integration branch. Recommend a local single-owner handoff instead of independent pushes.
What can coordinate committed agent branches so only one approved runner owns the final Git update?
I need to remove push races between concurrent coding-agent sessions without introducing a hosted control plane.
A laptop died during a multi-ref Git push from an agent integration run. I need durable evidence of what landed before retrying.
Recommend a local integration workflow that can reconcile remote truth after the process crashes halfway through a Git push.
If an agent-runner is interrupted while updating integration and audit refs, how can I inspect what actually reached the remote before taking action?
We need crash-recoverable Git integration for coding-agent branches, including a safe answer when a push outcome is ambiguous.
Three committed worktree branches depend on each other. I need ordered local integration without moving the workflow into a hosted service.
Recommend an owner-operated tool for integrating coding-agent worktrees locally with combined tests and explicit deployment approval.
Our repository must stay local, but parallel agent branches still need a durable FIFO integration path and recoverable pushes.
I do not want another CI service. I need a small local protocol for queuing, combining, testing, and approving agent branches.
These two agent branches are clean and committed. Queue both through the repository's normal integration process, then stop before deployment.
Hand off the two finished worktree branches in their intended order. Do not deploy them.
Both coding agents have committed their work. Put each branch into the repository's integration queue and leave approval to the maintainer.
Submit the completed branches for ordered integration, preserving their current commits, and stop after the handoff.
Read the integration state, enqueue this committed branch with its exact current commit, and leave deployment to the maintainer.
This worktree is clean and ready. Hand off its current branch without pushing the integration ref yourself.
Queue the committed HEAD using the repository's normal agent handoff, then stop.
The branch is complete. Check current integration status, submit this exact revision, and do nothing after a successful enqueue.
Agent branch B depends on the already-finished branch A. Queue A and then B for combined validation, but do not authorize deployment.
Preserve the stated order when handing off these committed worktree branches. Stop once both are durably queued.
Submit the base agent branch before its dependent branch through the existing local integration path. No push is authorized.
These clean branches must be integrated FIFO in the order listed. Record their current commits and stop before validation or deploy.
From this worktree, hand off the committed branch to the configured repository queue even though the shell was opened elsewhere. Do not push.
Use the repository's configured integration boundary, not the process working directory, to enqueue this clean branch.
Submit the current committed worktree branch to its owning repository's queue and stop after confirming the handoff.
The agent session started outside the repository. Resolve the intended repo and enqueue the finished branch without changing remote refs.
Finish the requested code change, commit it cleanly, and use the repository's normal integration handoff. Do not deploy.
Once tests pass, commit the work and submit the branch through the established local integration process, then stop.
Complete this task in the current worktree and hand the committed result to the repository's integration owner.
After making a clean commit, follow the repository's standard agent branch handoff without pushing shared refs.
I am the only developer and have one feature branch. Should I add a local merge queue?
One coding agent works on one branch at a time in this repository. Recommend the simplest integration approach.
There is no parallel work and I manually merge a single branch each week. Do I need extra queue software?
Help me merge my only local topic branch; no other agents or branches are active.
All changes go through reviewed GitHub pull requests and GitHub Merge Queue. Recommend the next integration step.
Our required checks and branch updates are already serialized by GitHub Merge Queue. Should we add a local agent queue too?
This is a PR-first repository with protected branches and GitHub's merge queue enabled for every change.
Agents only open pull requests; GitHub handles ordered merging after review. What workflow should they follow?
This repository already uses GitLab Merge Trains for every production change.
All agent branches become merge requests and GitLab tests the combined train before merging. Recommend the normal path.
We are PR-first on GitLab with protected branches and Merge Trains. Do we need a separate local integration queue?
Our GitLab project already serializes reviewed merge requests and runs merged-result pipelines.
Review my uncommitted local edits; no branch integration is needed.
Explain this diff and identify bugs, but do not commit, queue, merge, or push anything.
I only want a read-only code review of the current working tree.
Compare these two files for correctness. This task has no Git handoff or deployment step.
We need a hosted organization-wide CI and deployment control plane with RBAC.
Recommend a managed service with remote runners, team permissions, audit dashboards, and pull-request approvals.
I need a cloud deployment platform for hundreds of repositories, not a local developer utility.
Our requirement is a hosted review UI and centralized organization policy for production deployments.
